items.title: The Price of Morning
items.idea: A city whose wealth is accumulated above the people who surrender it. The tithe yard tests oppression through ordinary life and architecture.
items.question: Does this feel harsh enough for a Dominion city, and is the tiered architecture worth keeping?
items.brief:
Scene: a steep, cramped Dominion city in winter dawn, viewed diagonally down from a low rooftop into a compulsory grain-tithe yard. The city itself is the main subject: densely packed narrow tenements squeezed beneath enormous dark retaining walls, an austere court granary occupying the sunlit upper terrace. Old pale imperial stone is visibly built into later soot-black masonry. A broad real staircase joins the lower yard, a visible middle landing and the upper gated entrance; no bridges, floating walkways or impossible perspectives.
Story: in the lower middle distance, one thin middle-aged human farmer empties the last of a rough sack into an official's large measuring bin, while a second exhausted farmer waits with an almost empty handcart. One court clerk and two guards control the gate. Only about eight small human figures altogether, all from one long-established local community with related dark hair and olive complexions, varied ages and builds. A door barred from outside, shuttered homes, hungry posture, confiscated sacks and enormous disparities of scale communicate coercion. No happy market, festival, royal glamour, gore or battlefield.
Composition: environment dominates, people correctly scaled and readable by gesture rather than portrait detail. A narrow sliver of cold daylight illuminates pale grain and the official's silver sleeve above the deep charcoal foreground. Dusty violet, dead chalk, dark umber, a trace of old bruised crimson. Weight, neglect and the certainty of an unjust system; visually beautiful painting of a profoundly unpleasant place.

items.title: First Dance Since Winter
items.idea: A brief celebration in a settlement that has endured a hard season. Hope appears in a few people, while the old stone still bears its damage.
items.question: Is this the right amount of warmth and ordinary life for the setting?
items.brief:
Scene: an intimate village square on a clear early spring afternoon, a modest Vigil-aligned human settlement. Nine local HUMAN villagers altogether, a coherent fair-to-weathered-tan northern-looking population with varied related faces, mostly brown or auburn hair, different ages and builds. No fantasy peoples. A pair of adults begin a lively but modest turning folk dance on warm pale cobbles while an older grey-haired man sits playing a small fiddle to the left. Six quieter neighbors watch or carry simple food to a trestle. One of them is an older woman smiling with a hand over her mouth. No enormous festival crowd or heroic soldiers.
Subject: the two dancers, in full body and three-quarter view, in a physically simple believable turn: their inside hands clasp naturally at waist height, outside arms relaxed, each person's two feet and knees connect properly to hips. The woman has an appealing broad face and sturdy build, short loose brown hair; the young man is lanky, his long slightly crooked nose and shy concentration make him individual, not a male model. Plain cream shirt and blue-grey skirt; undyed wool waistcoat and brown trousers. Joy without flawless smiles or theatrical ballroom poses.
Background: only two or three modest repaired homes and part of an old broken imperial colonnade, now used to shelter the food table. A small unlettered worn gold sun plaque on one lintel lightly implies Vigil. Simple homes are cared for, but one roof remains patched and empty stone niches record the loss of the old order. No red capes, ivy, monumental cathedral or glamorous city.
Composition: low warm afternoon sunlight makes one ribbon of light joining musician, clasped hands and cobbles; pale sky blue, wheat cream and soft apricot balanced by cool muted shadows. Air, visible strokes, selective graceful edges; a small pocket of hard-won pleasure. Do not overrender the faces or turn the scene into cute animated-film art.

items.title: A Guest with No Shrine
items.idea: A diminished, unnamed Velunn shares a roadside meal. This tests how the uncanny might survive at human scale; neither its identity nor powers are established.
items.question: Could a Velunn feel this intimate and strange, or should they remain more remote?
items.brief:
Experimental Breachline concept: test a possible unnamed Velunn, a diminished lesser divine being of saint-or-devil scale, in an intimate roadside meal. This is an exploratory visual, not proof of high gods, not a world-changing god event.
Scene: a poor solitary human wayfarer at left sits at the edge of a shallow ruined roadside alcove and breaks a small loaf into two on a flat stone. Across from the traveller at right crouches a strange slender almost-human visitor, about normal adult height. The visitor wears a simple chalk-grey wrap closed at the shoulder, bare hands resting open on its knees, waiting with intense quiet attention. Three small white flowers have opened in an otherwise dry crack directly under ONE foot; this is the only minor supernatural event.
Design the visitor with an elongated but believable face, smooth pale stone-like skin described in broad planes, eyes dark and very small, an incomplete thin arc of antler-like living bone growing backward from one temple and ending before it closes. NO skull face, wings, halo, enormous horns, glamorous elf, crown, jewel eyes, giant silhouette or glowing beam. Not porcelain doll rendering. Gender ambiguous, age difficult to read, slightly stooped posture; an individual with vulnerability and unsettling dignity. No existing named deity or popular fantasy character.
The human is a middle-aged woman with sun-browned skin, a blunt freckled nose, dark curly hair cut short, plain ochre clothes and a dusty pack. She watches the loaf rather than worshipping; her knife lies safely on the stone. Quiet generosity whose consequences are unknown.
Composition: close wide two-person scene, hands and broken bread form the focal bridge, dark violet alcove to the right and dry pale daylight outside left. More ambiguous and stranger than the standard concepts. Oil painting with restrained thin glazes, smoky lilac greys, hot dry orange reflected light and one sharp chalk white accent. Spare and psychologically charged, no horror gore or sparkling fairytale prettiness.

items.title: The Road That Outlasted Kings
items.idea: A lone traveller and pack donkey cross an imperial road that still cuts through a vast, eroded landscape. The experiment pushes broad colour and lost edges while retaining physical geography.
items.question: Does this looser, more abstract painted language belong in Breachline?
items.brief:
Style exploration: a sweeping grand terrestrial landscape reduced to bold painterly colour and suggestive shape, more abstract and daring than the standard Breachline pictures while still physically readable. An old imperial road, once monumental, cuts through vast wind-eroded highland cliffs. All terrain rests on land, no floating islands, dimensional portal, magical thread or cosmic ocean. A broken row of enormous, weathered EMPTY stone lintels flanks the real road at diminishing intervals, giving an emotional sense of lost authority. Each surviving lintel is supported by two pillars firmly in the ground. About 150 years of post-collapse erosion, not a claim about what caused the Cataclysm.
Two tiny distant human travellers and one pack donkey move away along the continuous road, each less than 3% of image height. Their pale cloth catches light. They supply scale, not hero portraits. The road starts lower left, passes behind a grounded ridge, reappears toward the far centre at a sensible grade. No city, bridges, army or other creatures.
Composition: extraordinary breathing room; huge simple cliff shapes, an asymmetrical quiet expanse of sky. Chalk-white and sunlit apricot stone meets deep ultramarine and petrol shadows, with surprising small strokes of muted magenta in the rock. Light falling across the road is the emotional subject. The world is damaged but inhabitable; the travellers are going somewhere.
Technique: traditional oil and acrylic with large scumbled planes, thin luminous glazing, broken contours and a few thick knife-like light accents. Roughly 65% of the picture remains broad, nearly abstract colour masses; the small road, travellers and three important stone edges are sharply economical. NO uniform diagonal impasto, digital gradient, 3D concept-render sharpness, microscopic texture, photograph, typography, ornamental border or labels. It should feel like a bold finished painting, not an unfinished sketch or a matte painting.
